summary.intent: Plan and execute phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation unwrap consolidation), then run the full PR-QA pipeline (simplify, security-review, CodeRabbit CLI, push, PR creation, resolve CodeRabbit's GitHub review).
summary.outcome: Planning completed (5 plans / 3 waves / 6 requirements, plan-check passed after one revision round). Execution reached end of Wave 1 (49-01 SDK op, 49-02 useFolderNavigation) and dispatched Wave 2 (49-03 web single-item move); transcript cuts off before Wave 2 completes. PR-QA and PR creation not yet started.

repo: `reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange` (reencrypt.ts:49) is fully key-agnostic — takes raw key bytes with no owner/recipient distinction, directly reusable for the shared-folder move case.

File keys do NOT need re-registration after a folder move: `share_keys` entries are keyed by `itemId` (file UUID), not parent folder, so the download path resolves correctly regardless of where a file lives.

`adoptSharedFolderResult` must only be called once (for the source result) — calling it for the dest result corrupts the `sharedFolderTree` projection because it emits `sharedFolder:updated` with `live.ipnsName` filtered by `shareId` only.

Collision policy on `sdkCore.moveItem` is throw (`'An item with this name already exists in destination'`, sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:346) — no auto-rename needed, error propagates through `runWrite` → `p.setError`.
File IPNS key for re-encryption must come from `share_keys keyType:'file-ipns'`, NOT `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` — the latter is owner-wrapped and recipients cannot decrypt it.
Batch move is a web-layer pattern, not an SDK primitive: `useFileBrowserActions` loops single-item `client.moveItem`; the private `MoveDialog` already accepts an `items` prop.
Drag-and-drop move lives in `FileListItem` — `handleDragStart` is multi-select-aware, drops on folder rows call `handleDropOnFolder` → `moveItem`/`moveItems`.

SDK dist type declarations: `index.d.ts` is a barrel re-export; new class methods appear in `client.d.ts`. Web consumers see them through the barrel — the dist is valid even when `grep index.d.ts` shows nothing.
`useSharedWriteOps.test.ts` already exists — plan 49-03 extended it for `moveItemHandler` rather than creating a new test file.
`SharedFolderClient` Pick allowlist at shared-folder-projection.ts:28-38 must have `moveInSharedFolder` and `enumerateSharedSubtree` added — it only listed the 7 Phase 48 methods.

code.finding: reencryptFileMetadataForFolderChange is key-agnostic and reusable verbatim for the shared-folder move re-encryption path.
moveItem throws on name collision — caller does not need to handle auto-rename.
SharedFolderClient Pick allowlist — must be extended with moveInSharedFolder and enumerateSharedSubtree for phase 49.
Key resolution: k.keyType === 'file' && k.itemId === item.id — parent folder is irrelevant, proving file keys need no re-registration after a move.

workflow: Sequential executor (no worktrees) is preferred for AFK autonomous runs: parallel-worktree merge-back protocol is error-prone to hand-drive, and sequential execution avoids concurrent test processes starving RAM.
After new public SDK methods land, rebuild the SDK dist BEFORE dispatching web-layer plans — web `tsc` checks the built dist, not source, causing spurious type errors if stale.
GSD plan-checker is worth the iteration cost: it caught a real blocker (REQ-3 verify gate passed vacuously because no web unit test existed for the new handler).

CodeRabbit flow is two-stage: CLI review (`coderabbit review --agent`) runs before PR creation; after the PR is opened, CodeRabbit auto-posts a GitHub review that requires `/resolve-pr-reviews` to address.
The AI-SPEC keyword gate false-positives on 'eval' appearing in e2e requirement text — treat as non-blocking and proceed without AI-SPEC when there is no actual AI content.
Intel API surface regeneration can return empty (regex extractor unpopulated); it is a HINT-only artifact — RESEARCH.md with verified symbol refs is sufficient for the planner.
Scope expansions mid-planning (before the planner spawns) are cheap: update ROADMAP + CONTEXT, commit, then spawn planner with the expanded scope.

friction: git commit signing conflict: 1Password signer would wedge during unattended automated commits, requiring `commit.gpgsign=false` locally for the session. This creates a signed-rebase obligation before merge.
Plan-checker required a revision round: 2 blockers + 1 warning, one of which was a substantive gap (no web unit test for REQ-3 handler, making the verify gate vacuous).
False-positive on AI-SPEC gate: 'eval' in an e2e requirement string triggered the keyword scanner, requiring manual triage to confirm non-blocking.

Scope expansion arrived after research started: user added batch + drag move (previously out of scope) after the researcher was already dispatched, requiring ROADMAP + CONTEXT edits and a private-vault analog verification subagent before planning could proceed.

SDK dist staleness concern caused unnecessary investigation: new methods in `client.d.ts` were not visible in `index.d.ts` grep, leading to a dist-structure audit before confirming consumers see them through the barrel re-export.
